summary.text: 馬 depicts a horse as a whole animal; 马 is its standardized simplified form. The common meaning is “horse.”

formation.text: The traditional graph 馬 is pictographic: it depicts a horse, with features including an eye, mane, body, tail and legs. The graph is understood as a whole picture, not as a combination of separate semantic or phonetic parts.

history.text: The selected Shang-style oracle-bone and mid-Western Zhou bronze-style drawings show different historical forms of 馬, retaining recognizable features of the horse. They illustrate forms, not a proven line of descent; the earliest individual inscription is not dated here.
馬 is the traditional graph corresponding to simplified 马. The claim that 马 follows a cursive form is not established by the cited character-specific evidence.

uncertainties.text: The whole-animal pictograph analysis is supported, but the earliest dated inscription and earliest attested use of the word are unresolved. The account describing the head, mane, tail and four legs is a historical interpretation, not independent proof of the earliest graphic details.
“Big” and surname are recorded as senses, but their dates and any development from “horse” are not established here.

senses.text: The character’s common meaning is “horse.” The earliest lexical use is not dated here.
The character is also used as a surname. Its earliest attestation and relation to the word “horse” are unresolved.

limitations.text: Dated attestations for later senses and a supported path from “horse” to surname or other proposed extensions are not available here.

overview.text: 馬 pictures a horse as a whole animal. 马 is its standardized simplified form, and the common meaning is “horse.”

relationships.text: 馬 is the traditional graph corresponding to standardized simplified 马. The precise cursive pathway and its chronology are not established by the cited evidence.
